# Alpine A110 — Repair Manual (Type A 110, 1st edition October 1970)

> Front matter above this line is generated by `scripts/10_write_frontmatter.py` once the
> manifest exists — do not hand-edit it.

## What this manual is

The **factory repair manual** published by *Société des Automobiles ALPINE* (Epinay-sur-Seine
and Dieppe, France) for the **Alpine A110 "Berlinette"**, **1st edition, October 1970**.

This copy is an **English translation of the French original**, and the two documents in the
PDF are bound together:

| PDF pages | What it is |
|---|---|
| 1–60 | The repair manual proper — sections **A** through **R** |
| 61–87 | The **update supplement** (*mise à jour* / Technical Notes), carrying amendments dated **December 1970** and into **1971** |

The manual is organised by the factory's own **letter-number section codes** (`A-1`, `B-13`,
`N-4` …) printed in the page header, not by continuous page numbers. Citations in this wiki
give both: the section code and the PDF page.

## The car — background (best-effort, NOT from the manual; review pending)

The A110 is a rear-engined, rear-drive sports coupé: a polyester (fibreglass) body on a
central steel backbone chassis, with Renault running gear. Built 1961–1977; this manual covers
the **"model 70"** versions and later. It is the car that won the inaugural 1973 World Rally
Championship.

The manual's own `A-1` page states the four versions it covers:

| Version | Factory type | Engine type (per the manual) |
|---|---|---|
| "85" | 1300 VC | 810-30 — derived from Renault 810-03 (R1192) |
| 1300 G | 1300 VA | 812-00 family — Renault 8 Gordini derived |
| 1300 S | 1300 VB | 812-00 derived — Renault 8 Gordini |
| 1600 S | 1600 VB | 807-25 — derived from 807-01, Renault 16 TS |

plus the **GS engine option** (competition version).

Rough figures from general (non-manual) sources, for orientation only — **not** manual data:
1289 cc / ~81 hp (V85), ~1255 cc / ~103 hp (1300 G), 1296 cc / ~120 hp (1300 S),
1565 cc / ~138 hp (1600 S).

## What the manual covers

The section letters, as printed on the contents plate:

| Code | Section (as translated) | French original | PDF pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | General / characteristics | Généralités | 7–9 |
| B | Engine & ignition | Moteur · Allumage | 10–25 |
| C | Electrical equipment | Équipement électrique | 26–28 |
| D | Clutch | Embrayage | 29–32 |
| E | Gearbox | Boîte de vitesses | 33–38 |
| G | Steering | Direction | 39–40 |
| H | Front axle / front suspension | Train avant | 41–45 |
| J | Rear axle | Train arrière | 46–47 |
| L | Suspension & dampers | Suspension · Amortisseurs | 48–49 |
| M | Braking system | Freinage | 50–51 |
| N | Bodywork | Carrosserie | 52–58 |
| R | Special tooling | Outillage spécial | 59 |

The update supplement (61–87) re-issues amendments against those same chapters, plus the
**wiring-harness / connector directory** ("Directory of Failures" — *répertoire des faisceaux*)
on pages 64–72 and **paint and polyurethane lacquer compositions** on 76–77.

## What it does NOT cover

- **This scan is abridged.** Many section-code pages are simply absent: `D-1`, `E-2`, `E-3`,
  `G-2` onward, `J-1`, `L-2` onward, `M-1`, and `N-6` through `N-13` (the supplement cites
  `N-13`, so it existed). Expect gaps mid-chapter; they are a property of the source, not
  something this conversion can fix.
- **It is not a standalone manual.** Section R states outright that, apart from one spark-plug
  wrench for the 1600 S, *no tooling beyond that for Renault 8, 10 and 16 is needed* — and the
  engines, gearbox and much of the running gear are Renault units. For engine internals you
  will often need the corresponding **Renault** workshop manual.
- No owner/driver content, no parts catalogue, no later A110 1600 SC/SX material (post-1973).

## Provenance caveats — read before trusting a number

1. **It is a machine translation.** Section titles alone show the quality: "MOTOR ALLUMAGE",
   "BOX OF VITSES" (*boîte de vitesses*), "ARRIER TRAIN", "AMORISTS" (*amortisseurs*),
   "DIRECTORATE" for *direction* (steering). French terms survive untranslated throughout.
2. **Numbers may have been mangled twice** — once by OCR of the French scan, once by the
   translation. French decimal **commas** appear inconsistently as periods: the same overall
   length shows as both `3.850` and `3.85 m` on page A-2. **Every torque, clearance and
   capacity in this wiki must be treated as provisional** and verified against the rendered
   PDF page before it is used on a car.
3. **Pages 64–72 are unreadable as text.** The harness tables have 90°-rotated column headers;
   the translation overlay scrambles them completely. They are delivered as **images only** —
   never transcribed.
4. The PDF has a usable text layer already (no re-OCR was needed), but it is the *translation's*
   text layer, so item 2 applies to all of it.
